extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, researchers, and professionals seeking descriptions of U.S. federal agencies and their statutory missions
extracted.subtask_description: Directory-style listings of U.S. federal agencies with short descriptions of statutory missions, duties, authorities, and program purposes. Useful for identifying what each agency is charged to do and what programs or responsibilities it administers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Services Corporation mission and funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Is funded through congressional appropriations and provides legal services through grants to independent local programs selected through a system of competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library of Congress responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Library of Congress is the national library of the United States, offering diverse materials for research including the world's most extensive collections in many areas such as American history, music, and law. The Librarian, appointed by the President with the advice and consent of the Senate, directs the Library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope of responsibility widened by subsequent legislation (2 U.S.C. 131-168d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Local Television Loan Guarantee Board purpose and authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Established to guarantee loans to facilitate access, on a technologically neutral basis, to signals of local television stations for households located in non-served areas or underserved areas; authorized to approve guarantees up to 80 percent of the principal amount of up to $1.25 billion in loans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board's authority to guarantee loans under the Program expires on the earlier of the date the Secretary of Agriculture determines that at least 75 percent of Designated Market Areas (other than the top 40 DMAs) have access to Local Television Broadcast Signals for virtually all households or December 31, 2006.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Management and Budget functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates, formulates, and coordinates management procedures and program objectives within and among Federal departments and agencies; controls the administration of the Federal budget and provides the President with recommendations regarding budget proposals and relevant legislative enactments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marine Mammal Commission primary duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Charged with duties including: (1) review and study of U.S. activities pursuant to laws and international conventions relating to marine mammals; (2) continuing review of the condition of marine mammal stocks and methods for their protection and conservation and of applications for permits; (3) undertake necessary studies; (4) recommend steps for protection and conservation to the Secretary and other federal officials; (5) recommend appropriate international policies to the Secretary of State; (6) recommend revisions of endangered and threatened species lists with regard to marine mammals; and (7) recommend additional measures to further the policies of the Act including provisions for protection of indigenous peoples whose livelihood may be adversely affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also carries out a small research program to support conservation and protection goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maritime Administration (MARAD) program objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs of the Maritime Administration promote the development and maintenance of an adequate, well-balanced United States merchant marine sufficient to carry domestic and a substantial portion of foreign waterborne commerce and capable of service as a naval and military auxiliary in time of war or national emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also seeks to ensure adequate shipbuilding and repair services, efficient ports, effective inter-modal transportation systems, and reserve shipping capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medicare Payment Advisory Commission (MedPAC) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: An independent Congressional agency to advise the U.S. Congress on issues affecting the Medicare program, including payments to private health plans and providers, and to analyze access to care, quality of care, and other issues affecting Medicare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Systems Protection Board mission and functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Serves as the guardian of Federal merit systems; protects Federal merit systems and the rights of individuals within those systems by adjudicating individual employee appeals, conducting merit systems studies, and reviewing significant actions of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM).

rubrics_metrics.name: Military Compensation and Retirement Modernization Commission duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct a review of military compensation and retirement systems and make recommendations to modernize such systems to ensure the long-term viability of the All-Volunteer Force, enable quality of life for members and families, and modernize and achieve fiscal sustainability for compensation and retirement systems for the 21st century.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tasked to submit a report containing a comprehensive study and recommendations by May 1, 2014, including detailed findings, conclusions, and recommendations for legislation and administrative actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) purpose and grant policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms partnerships with poor countries committed to good governance, economic freedom and investments in their citizens and provides well-performing countries with large-scale grants to fund country-led solutions for reducing poverty through sustainable economic growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MCC grants complement other U.S. and international development programs and are implemented through compacts and threshold programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible for safety and health in the Nation's mines: develops and promulgates mandatory safety and health standards, ensures compliance, assesses civil penalties for violations, investigates accidents, cooperates with States on mine safety programs, improves and expands training programs, and contributes to mine safety and health research and development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All activities are aimed at preventing and reducing mine accidents and occupational diseases in the mining industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minerals Management Service (MMS) role
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses the nature, extent, recoverability, and value of leasable minerals on the Outer Continental Shelf; ensures orderly and timely inventory and development and efficient recovery of mineral resources; encourages utilization of the best available and safest technology; and safeguards against fraud, waste, and abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MMS was renamed and reorganized into successor bureaus (BOEM, BSEE) in later years.

rubrics_metrics.name: United States Bureau of Mines (USBM) functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Primarily a research and fact-finding agency to provide technology for the extraction, processing, use, and recycling of the Nation’s nonfuel mineral resources at reasonable cost without harm to the environment or workers; collected, compiled, analyzed, and published statistical and economic information on nonfuel mineral resource development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USBM was terminated in 1996 with certain functions transferred to the Secretary of Energy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minority Business Development Agency (MBDA) mission and services
rubrics_metrics.description: Develops and coordinates a national program for minority business enterprise to assist minority businesses in achieving effective and equitable participation in the American free enterprise system; provides national policies and leadership and business development services via minority business opportunity committees, development centers, and electronic commerce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promotes and coordinates efforts of Federal agencies to assist minority businesses and coordinates opportunities in the private sector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Minority Economic Impact (OMEI) objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Build effective partnerships between the Department and minority institutions, increase the capabilities of such institutions to compete effectively for grants and contracts, and increase their participation in Department programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mississippi River Commission duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend policy and work on flood control, navigation, and environmental projects affecting the Mississippi River; study and report on necessity for modifications to river operations; conduct semiannual inspection trips and public hearings along the river.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent is to lead sustainable management and development of water-related resources for the nation’s benefit and people’s well-being.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morris K. Udall and Stewart L. Udall Foundation purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase awareness of the importance of the nation's natural resources; foster recognition and understanding of the role of the environment and public lands in U.S. development; identify critical environmental issues; develop resources to train professionals in environmental and related fields; provide educational outreach; develop resources to train Native American and Alaska Native professionals in health care and public policy; provide assessment, mediation, and related services to resolve environmental disputes involving federal agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foundation was established by Congress in 1992 and later renamed to include Stewart Udall.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASA mission statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The mission of the National Aeronautics and Space Administration is to pioneer the future in space exploration, scientific discovery, and aeronautics research.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Agricultural Library (NAL) role
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary resource in the United States for information about food, agriculture, and natural resources; serves as an electronic gateway to scientific literature, printed text, and agricultural images; serves USDA and a broad customer base including policymakers, agricultural specialists, research scientists, and the general public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works with other agricultural libraries and institutions to advance open and democratic access to agricultural information.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepares estimates and reports on production, supply, price, chemical use, and other items necessary for the orderly operation of the U.S. agricultural economy using complex sample surveys; conducts the Census of Agriculture every 5 years; performs reimbursable survey work and statistical consulting services and provides technical assistance for developing agricultural data systems in other countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports cover various commodities and farm statistics and are produced using mail, telephone, interviews, and field visits.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Safeguards and preserves the records of the Government, ensures public discovery and use of documentary heritage, establishes policies and procedures for managing U.S. Government records, manages the Presidential Libraries system, and publishes laws, regulations, and Presidential and other public documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Assessment Governing Board (NAGB) authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Created to set policy for the National Assessment of Educational Progress (NAEP); identifies subjects to be tested, determines content and achievement levels for each assessment, approves all test questions, and takes steps to improve reporting of results; responsible for communicating NAEP results to a wide range of audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Bankruptcy Review Commission mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate and study issues relating to the Bankruptcy Code; solicit divergent views of parties concerned with the operation of the bankruptcy system; evaluate advisability of proposals; prepare a report to the President, Congress and the Chief Justice; commission was terminated after submitting its final report.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Biological Service (NBS) mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the scientific understanding and technologies needed to support sound management and conservation of the Nation's biological resources by undertaking research, inventory, monitoring, information sharing, and technology transfer activities; establish partnerships with Federal, State, and local agencies, museums, universities, and private organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides essential scientific support, technical assistance, and information required for sound management and policy decisions regarding biological resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Bipartisan Commission on the Future of Medicare purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Study the future of Medicare including Medicare and the baby boomers, the health needs of an aging population, multigenerational perspectives, and America in the next century.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Capital Planning Commission role
rubrics_metrics.description: Central agency for conducting planning and development activities for Federal lands and facilities in the National Capital Region; established as a park planning agency and later designated the central planning agency for Federal and D.C. governments.
